data.title: Tabs
data.tagline: Switch between a few peer sections on the same page
data.description: Tabs work for sections such as Overview, Settings, and Logs under the same object. Keep the active tab obvious and decide whether unfinished input remains when switching. If the sections are really separate destinations, use navigation instead.

use: Separate content that shares the same context
avoid: Use tabs for the product's main navigation
Create so many tabs that they no longer fit
Hide required steps behind optional-looking tabs
Discard unsaved input silently when switching

lessonPractice.title: A project detail page switches among Overview, Members, and Logs, all within the current project. How should it be organized?

options.label: Use tabs for the three peer sections and mark the active one
options.feedback: The sections share one project context and the same level, so tabs preserve context while switching content.

options.label: Add all three destinations to the global top navigation
options.feedback: Global navigation serves major destinations across the site, not sections inside one project.

options.label: Turn them into three steps that must be completed in order
options.feedback: Overview, Members, and Logs have no completion order, so steps would invent a false workflow.

data.agentPrompt: Use tabs for Overview, Members, and Logs inside project details and always show the active tab. Preserve appropriate section state and test mouse, keyboard, and narrow-screen behavior.
